countries.title: Czechia
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Czech cuisine is built on rich sauces, dumplings, and pork — food meant to carry you through a long workday, not just look good in a photo.
countries.taste_intro: Plenty of bread and potato dumplings, plenty of creamy, spiced sauces, and beer as a natural part of the table, not an exception.

traditional_dishes.name: Czech Beef Sirloin in Cream Sauce (Svíčková)
traditional_dishes.note: Beef with root vegetables in a creamy sauce, served with a bread dumpling.

traditional_dishes.name: Czech Roast Pork with Dumpling and Sauerkraut (Vepřo Knedlo Zelo)
traditional_dishes.note: Roast pork, dumpling, and cabbage — a classic Sunday lunch.

traditional_dishes.name: Tomato sauce with beef
traditional_dishes.note: A sweet-and-sour tomato sauce with beef, a favorite with kids.

must_try.name: Czech Beef Sirloin in Cream Sauce (Svíčková)
must_try.note: The best-known Czech sauce — root vegetables, cream, and a bread dumpling.

must_try.name: Czech Roast Pork with Dumpling and Sauerkraut (Vepřo Knedlo Zelo)
must_try.note: A Sunday classic: roast pork, dumpling, and cabbage.

must_try.name: Kulajda (South Bohemian Sour Cream and Mushroom Soup)
must_try.note: A tangy creamy soup with potatoes, mushrooms, and egg.

must_try.name: Bramboráky (Czech Potato Pancakes)
must_try.note: Fried potato pancakes with marjoram and garlic.

must_try.name: Czech Sweet Buns
must_try.note: Yeasted pastry filled with curd cheese, poppy seed, or plum jam.

fun_facts: Czechia is one of the countries with the highest beer consumption per capita in the world, and beer is commonly drunk with lunch too.
The word "knedlík" has no exact English equivalent — the closest is "dumpling," but the bread dumpling is unique in its texture.
countries.seo_title: Czechia — Czech cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover Czech cuisine: svíčková, roast pork with dumpling and cabbage, kulajda, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Slovakia
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Slovak cuisine grows out of mountains and pastures — bryndza cheese, potatoes, and cabbage come together into a hearty, warming kitchen.
countries.taste_intro: Salty sheep's-milk bryndza, smoked meat, and sauerkraut — Slovak food is bold and never apologizes for being filling.

traditional_dishes.name: Bryndzové Halušky (Slovak Potato Dumplings with Sheep's Cheese)
traditional_dishes.note: Potato dumplings with sheep's-milk bryndza and bacon — Slovakia's national dish.

traditional_dishes.name: Kapustnica (Slovak Sauerkraut and Smoked Meat Soup)
traditional_dishes.note: A Christmas cabbage soup with smoked meat and dried mushrooms.

traditional_dishes.name: Segedin goulash
traditional_dishes.note: Pork with sauerkraut and sour cream, popular with neighboring countries too.

must_try.name: Bryndzové Halušky (Slovak Potato Dumplings with Sheep's Cheese)
must_try.note: Potato dumplings with bryndza cheese and fried bacon.

must_try.name: Kapustnica (Slovak Sauerkraut and Smoked Meat Soup)
must_try.note: Sauerkraut soup with sausage and mushrooms.

must_try.name: Lokše (Slovak Potato Flatbread)
must_try.note: Thin potato flatbreads, savory or sweet.

must_try.name: Pirohy with bryndza
must_try.note: Boiled dumplings filled with bryndza cheese and potato.

must_try.name: Demikát (Slovak Potato and Mushroom Soup)
must_try.note: Potato soup with dried mushrooms and cream.

fun_facts: Bryndzové halušky are officially protected as a traditional Slovak specialty product under the EU's protection scheme.
Bryndza is traditionally made from sheep's milk and matures only in the mountain regions of northern Slovakia.
countries.seo_title: Slovakia — Slovak cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover Slovak cuisine: bryndzové halušky, kapustnica, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Poland
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Polish cuisine combines sauerkraut, mushrooms, and yeasted dough into food built for long winters and family Sundays.
countries.taste_intro: Tanginess and smokiness run through almost everything in Polish cooking, from żurek to bigos, which only gets better the longer it simmers.

traditional_dishes.name: Pierogi Ruskie (Polish Potato and Curd Cheese Dumplings)
traditional_dishes.note: Dumplings filled with potato and curd cheese, served with fried onion.

traditional_dishes.name: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
traditional_dishes.note: A hunter's stew of sauerkraut and several kinds of meat.

traditional_dishes.name: Żurek (Polish Sour Rye Soup)
traditional_dishes.note: A sour rye soup with sausage and egg.

must_try.name: Pierogi Ruskie (Polish Potato and Curd Cheese Dumplings)
must_try.note: Boiled dumplings with potato, curd cheese, and fried onion.

must_try.name: Bigos (Polish Hunter's Stew)
must_try.note: A rich stew of sauerkraut and meat, best on the second day.

must_try.name: Żurek (Polish Sour Rye Soup)
must_try.note: A sour soup often served in a hollowed-out loaf of bread.

must_try.name: Gołąbki (Polish Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
must_try.note: Cabbage rolls filled with meat and rice in tomato sauce.

must_try.name: Placki Ziemniaczane (Polish Potato Pancakes)
must_try.note: Fried potato pancakes, similar to Czech bramboráky.

fun_facts: Bigos is traditionally cooked in large batches in Polish households and reheated for days — it's said to only get better with time.
Żurek is often served in a hollowed-out loaf of bread instead of a bowl.
countries.seo_title: Poland — Polish cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover Polish cuisine: pierogi, bigos, żurek, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Germany
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: German cuisine varies widely by region, but a love of meat, potatoes, and a good sauce runs through all of it.
countries.taste_intro: Tangy meat in a rich sauce, crackling pork skin, curry spice on a quick street-food classic — Germany does both the Sunday roast and street food equally well.

traditional_dishes.name: Sauerbraten (German Marinated Pot Roast)
traditional_dishes.note: Beef marinated for several days, then braised until tender.

traditional_dishes.name: Schweinshaxe (German Roasted Pork Knuckle)
traditional_dishes.note: Roasted pork knuckle with crackling skin.

traditional_dishes.name: Currywurst (Berlin Sausage with Curry Ketchup)
traditional_dishes.note: Grilled sausage with a ketchup-curry sauce, a Berlin street classic.

must_try.name: Sauerbraten (German Marinated Pot Roast)
must_try.note: Marinated beef braised in a tangy root-vegetable sauce.

must_try.name: Schweinshaxe (German Roasted Pork Knuckle)
must_try.note: Roasted pork knuckle served with beer and a dumpling.

must_try.name: Currywurst (Berlin Sausage with Curry Ketchup)
must_try.note: Grilled sausage with curry-ketchup sauce.

must_try.name: Kartoffelpuffer (German Potato Pancakes)
must_try.note: Fried potato pancakes, usually served with applesauce.

must_try.name: Königsberger Klopse (German Meatballs in Caper Sauce)
must_try.note: Meatballs in a white caper sauce.

fun_facts: Germany has more than 1,500 types of sausage, and over 70 million currywursts are eaten in Berlin alone every year.
Sauerbraten is traditionally marinated for up to a week — recipes vary widely from region to region.
countries.seo_title: Germany — German cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover German cuisine: sauerbraten, schweinshaxe, currywurst, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Austria
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Austrian cuisine combines Viennese elegance with Alpine heartiness — from the fried schnitzel to sweet Sunday dumplings.
countries.taste_intro: Crispy fried meat, broth-based soups with meat, and an endless range of desserts — Austria takes dessert as seriously as the main course.

traditional_dishes.name: Wiener Schnitzel (Viennese Breaded Veal Cutlet)
traditional_dishes.note: Breaded fried veal cutlet, a classic of Viennese cuisine.

traditional_dishes.name: Tafelspitz (Viennese Boiled Beef)
traditional_dishes.note: Boiled beef from broth with apple and chive horseradish.

traditional_dishes.name: Sachertorte (Original Viennese Chocolate Cake)
traditional_dishes.note: A chocolate cake with apricot filling from Vienna's Hotel Sacher.

must_try.name: Wiener Schnitzel
must_try.note: Breaded fried veal cutlet with a slice of lemon.

must_try.name: Tafelspitz (Viennese Boiled Beef)
must_try.note: Boiled beef from a quality broth with horseradish sauce.

must_try.name: Kaiserschmarrn (Austrian Shredded Pancake)
must_try.note: A torn sweet omelet with raisins and powdered sugar.

must_try.name: Sachertorte (Original Viennese Chocolate Cake)
must_try.note: A dense chocolate cake with an apricot layer.

must_try.name: Tyrolean dumplings
must_try.note: Savory dumplings made from stale bread and bacon.

fun_facts: The original Sachertorte recipe is still kept secret, and a legal dispute over the "true" version ran between Viennese pastry shops for decades.
By tradition, a real Wiener Schnitzel is always veal — made with pork, it's a "schnitzel Viennese style," not a true Wiener Schnitzel.
countries.seo_title: Austria — Austrian cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover Austrian cuisine: Wiener Schnitzel, Tafelspitz, Sachertorte, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Hungary
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Hungarian cuisine is built on paprika — ground, sweet, and hot — which colors soups, sauces, and braised meats a deep red.
countries.taste_intro: Smoky sweet paprika, onion, and lard form the base of nearly every Hungarian dish, from goulash soup to chicken paprikash.

traditional_dishes.name: Hungarian Goulash Soup (Gulyás)
traditional_dishes.note: A beef soup with potatoes and ground paprika — the origin of the word "goulash."

traditional_dishes.name: Chicken Paprikash (Paprikás Csirke)
traditional_dishes.note: Chicken in a creamy paprika sauce with dumplings.

traditional_dishes.name: Lángos (Hungarian Fried Dough)
traditional_dishes.note: Fried yeasted dough with garlic, sour cream, and cheese.

must_try.name: Hungarian Goulash Soup (Gulyás)
must_try.note: A beef soup with paprika, potatoes, and caraway.

must_try.name: Chicken Paprikash (Paprikás Csirke)
must_try.note: Chicken in a paprika sauce with sour cream.

must_try.name: Lángos (Hungarian Fried Dough)
must_try.note: Fried dough with garlic water, sour cream, and cheese.

must_try.name: Halászlé (Hungarian Fisherman's Soup)
must_try.note: A fiery fish soup made with carp, typical along the Danube and Tisza.

must_try.name: Dobos Torte (Hungarian Caramel-Topped Layer Cake)
must_try.note: A layered sponge cake with a caramel top.

fun_facts: Hungarian distinguishes "gulyás" (a soup) from "pörkölt" (a thicker braised meat dish) — what many other countries call goulash is usually pörkölt in Hungary.
Sweet paprika is grown mainly around the towns of Kalocsa and Szeged, both of which hold protected designation-of-origin status.
countries.seo_title: Hungary — Hungarian cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover Hungarian cuisine: gulyás, chicken paprikash, lángos, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Italy
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Italian cuisine rests on simplicity and the quality of its ingredients, not on complicated technique.
countries.taste_intro: Few ingredients, but the best you can find — ripe tomatoes, good olive oil, fresh herbs.

traditional_dishes.name: Pizza Margherita
traditional_dishes.note: Thin dough, tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil — in the colors of the Italian flag.

traditional_dishes.name: Spaghetti Carbonara
traditional_dishes.note: Eggs, guanciale, and pecorino — no cream.

traditional_dishes.name: Risotto alla Milanese (Milanese Saffron Risotto)
traditional_dishes.note: Saffron risotto, the traditional side to ossobuco.

must_try.name: Spaghetti Carbonara
must_try.note: A Roman classic of just four ingredients: egg, guanciale, pecorino, and pepper.

must_try.name: Pizza Margherita
must_try.note: Neapolitan pizza with tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil.

must_try.name: Risotto alla Milanese (Milanese Saffron Risotto)
must_try.note: Creamy saffron risotto from Lombardy.

must_try.name: Lasagne alla Bolognese
must_try.note: Layered pasta with meat ragù and béchamel.

must_try.name: Ossobuco alla Milanese (Braised Veal Shank)
must_try.note: Braised veal shank with gremolata.

fun_facts: "Al dente" literally means "to the tooth" — pasta is never cooked until mushy.
Under AVPN certification, a true Neapolitan pizza may only use a limited set of approved ingredients and must be baked in a wood-fired oven.
countries.seo_title: Italy — Italian cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover Italian cuisine: typical ingredients, traditional dishes, and tried-and-tested recipes.

countries.title: France
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: French cuisine gave the world its foundational cooking techniques — and yet, at heart, it remains rural, built on braised meat and good wine.
countries.taste_intro: Butter, wine, and long braising — French classics never rush, flavor builds slowly, layer by layer.

traditional_dishes.name: Beef Bourguignon (Bœuf Bourguignon)
traditional_dishes.note: Beef braised in red wine with mushrooms and bacon.

traditional_dishes.name: Ratatouille (Provençal Stewed Vegetables)
traditional_dishes.note: Braised vegetables from Provence — eggplant, zucchini, pepper, tomato.

traditional_dishes.name: Quiche Lorraine (French Bacon and Egg Tart)
traditional_dishes.note: A savory tart with bacon, egg, and cream.

must_try.name: Bœuf bourguignon
must_try.note: Beef braised in red wine, Burgundy style.

must_try.name: Coq au vin
must_try.note: Rooster (or chicken) braised in wine with mushrooms and bacon.

must_try.name: Ratatouille (Provençal Stewed Vegetables)
must_try.note: Braised Provençal vegetables.

must_try.name: Quiche Lorraine (French Bacon and Egg Tart)
must_try.note: A savory tart with bacon and egg custard.

must_try.name: Crêpes (French Thin Pancakes)
must_try.note: Thin pancakes, savory or sweet.

fun_facts: French gastronomy is inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list as an entire social ritual of dining.
Bœuf bourguignon began as food for Burgundy's winemakers — tougher cuts of beef tenderized by long braising in the local wine.
countries.seo_title: France — French cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover French cuisine: bœuf bourguignon, ratatouille, quiche Lorraine, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Spain
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Spanish cuisine is a cuisine of sharing — small tapas plates, large pans of paella, all enjoyed at a table with family and friends.
countries.taste_intro: Saffron, garlic, olive oil, and fresh seafood — salty and briny on the coast, heartier inland, with cured meats and legumes.

traditional_dishes.name: Paella Valenciana
traditional_dishes.note: Saffron rice with chicken, rabbit, and beans from Valencia.

traditional_dishes.name: Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelet)
traditional_dishes.note: A dense omelet of potato and onion.

traditional_dishes.name: Gazpacho
traditional_dishes.note: A cold tomato soup from Andalusia.

must_try.name: Paella Valenciana
must_try.note: Saffron rice with meat and beans, cooked in a wide pan.

must_try.name: Tortilla Española (Spanish Potato Omelet)
must_try.note: A dense potato omelet, a tapas classic.

must_try.name: Gazpacho
must_try.note: A cold tomato soup, refreshing in the summer heat.

must_try.name: Patatas Bravas
must_try.note: Fried potatoes with a spicy tomato sauce and aioli.

must_try.name: Croquetas de Jamón (Spanish Ham Croquettes)
must_try.note: Fried croquettes with a ham béchamel filling.

fun_facts: A true Paella Valenciana traditionally contains no seafood — that belongs to coastal variants like paella de marisco.
The word "tapas" likely comes from the custom of covering a glass of wine with a slice of bread or ham to keep insects out.
countries.seo_title: Spain — Spanish cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti
countries.meta_description: Discover Spanish cuisine: paella, tortilla Española, gazpacho, and more traditional recipes step by step.

countries.title: Portugal
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Portuguese cuisine belongs to the sea — cod, sardines, and shellfish, rounded out with olive oil and fresh herbs.
countries.taste_intro: Dried salt cod (bacalhau) is so central that people say there's a recipe for every day of the year — a salty, smoky flavor nothing else replaces.

traditional_dishes.name: Bacalhau à Brás (Portuguese Shredded Salt Cod)
traditional_dishes.note: Shredded salt cod with matchstick fries and eggs.

traditional_dishes.name: Caldo Verde (Portuguese Kale Soup)
traditional_dishes.note: A kale soup with chouriço sausage.

traditional_dishes.name: Pastéis de Nata (Portuguese Custard Tarts)
traditional_dishes.note: Crisp pastry cups with an egg custard filling.

must_try.name: Bacalhau à Brás (Portuguese Shredded Salt Cod)
must_try.note: Shredded salt cod baked with matchstick fries and eggs.

must_try.name: Caldo Verde (Portuguese Kale Soup)
must_try.note: A kale soup with sausage, typical of the north.

must_try.name: Pastéis de Nata (Portuguese Custard Tarts)
must_try.note: Crisp pastry cups with caramelized egg custard.

must_try.name: Arroz de Marisco (Portuguese Seafood Rice)
must_try.note: Seafood rice with shrimp and mussels.

must_try.name: Francesinha (Porto Sandwich in Beer Sauce)
must_try.note: A hearty meat-and-cheese sandwich covered in a beer sauce.

fun_facts: It's said that Portugal has more than a thousand different recipes for dried salt cod (bacalhau).
Pastéis de nata are traditionally baked in Lisbon to a strictly guarded recipe from the Pastéis de Belém monastery bakery.
countries.seo_title: Portugal — Portuguese cuisine, recipes, and traditional dishes | Atlas Chuti

countries.title: Greece
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Greek cuisine forms the foundation of what we now call the Mediterranean diet — olive oil, vegetables, lamb, and plenty of shared plates.
countries.taste_intro: Lemon, oregano, and olive oil turn up in nearly every other dish, alongside salty feta and cooling yogurt-based tzatziki against the summer heat.

traditional_dishes.name: Moussaka
traditional_dishes.note: Baked eggplant with ground meat and béchamel.

traditional_dishes.name: Souvlaki (Greek Grilled Skewers)
traditional_dishes.note: Grilled meat skewers served in pita bread.

traditional_dishes.name: Tzatziki
traditional_dishes.note: A yogurt sauce with cucumber and garlic.

must_try.name: Moussaka
must_try.note: Layered baked eggplant with meat and béchamel.

must_try.name: Souvlaki (Greek Grilled Skewers)
must_try.note: Grilled meat skewers with pita bread and tzatziki.

must_try.name: Tzatziki
must_try.note: A cooling yogurt sauce with cucumber and garlic.

must_try.name: Spanakopita (Greek Spinach Pie)
must_try.note: A crisp spinach-and-feta pie in phyllo pastry.

must_try.name: Greek salad
must_try.note: Tomato, cucumber, feta, and olives, without a dressing.

fun_facts: A true Greek salad (horiatiki) is traditionally made without lettuce — just tomato, cucumber, onion, olives, and a slab of feta.
Under EU protected-designation rules, feta may only come from Greece and must be made from sheep's or goat's milk.

countries.intro: Croatian cuisine has two faces: Mediterranean on the coast, with fish and olive oil, and Central European inland, with meat and dumplings.
countries.taste_intro: Olive oil, garlic, and fresh fish rule the Adriatic coast, while braised meat, cabbage, and stuffed dishes dominate inland — both share a taste for slow cooking.

traditional_dishes.name: Pašticada (Dalmatian Braised Beef)
traditional_dishes.note: Beef braised in wine with prunes and spices, from Split and Dalmatia.

traditional_dishes.name: Croatian Black Risotto (Crni Rižot)
traditional_dishes.note: Black risotto with cuttlefish and their ink.

traditional_dishes.name: Peka (Croatian Under-the-Bell Roast)
traditional_dishes.note: Meat and vegetables slow-roasted under a bell-shaped lid in embers.

must_try.name: Pašticada (Dalmatian Braised Beef)
must_try.note: Dalmatian beef braised in wine, traditionally with prune jam.

must_try.name: Crni rižot

must_try.name: Peka (Croatian Under-the-Bell Roast)
must_try.note: Meat and vegetables slow-roasted under the peka lid.

must_try.name: Zagorski Štrukli (Croatian Cottage Cheese Rolls)
must_try.note: Cheese-filled dumplings from the northern Zagorje region.

must_try.name: Fritule (Croatian Fried Doughnuts)
must_try.note: Small yeasted doughnuts with raisins and lemon zest.

fun_facts: "Peka" is both the name of the dish and of the cast-iron lid under which meat and vegetables are slow-roasted in the embers.
Pašticada is traditionally marinated up to two days in advance, which gives it its depth of flavor.

countries.intro: Slovenian cuisine is small but varied — Alpine, Mediterranean, and Pannonian traditions all meet within one small country.
countries.taste_intro: Plenty of yeasted dough filled sweet and savory, alongside cabbage, potatoes, and, in the mountains, smoked meat — a cozy, rural flavor.

traditional_dishes.name: Kranjska Klobasa (Carniolan Sausage)
traditional_dishes.note: A protected Slovenian sausage, a symbol of the national cuisine.

traditional_dishes.name: Potica (Slovenian Nut Roll)

must_try.name: Jota (Slovenian Sauerkraut and Bean Soup)

must_try.name: Štruklji (Slovenian Cottage Cheese Rolls)

countries.intro: Serbian cuisine is a cuisine of the grill and the family feast — grilled meat, stuffed vegetables, and sweet layered pastries to finish.
countries.taste_intro: Grilled ground meat with onion and fresh bread is Serbia's take on fast food, alongside cabbage stuffed with meat and rice for Sunday.

traditional_dishes.name: Pljeskavica (Serbian Grilled Meat Patty)
traditional_dishes.note: A large grilled meat patty, Serbia's take on the hamburger.

traditional_dishes.name: Sarma (Serbian Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
traditional_dishes.note: Cabbage rolls filled with meat and rice, a traditional Christmas dish.

must_try.name: Ćevapi (Balkan Grilled Meat Rolls)
must_try.note: Grilled ground-meat rolls with onion and ajvar.

countries.title: Romania
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Romanian cuisine draws on Balkan, Slavic, and Hungarian influences — the result is a kitchen full of stuffed vegetables, cornmeal porridge, and braised meat.
countries.taste_intro: Cornmeal porridge (mămăligă) stands in for both bread and potatoes, meat comes with plenty of dill and sour cream, and sweet curd-cheese dumplings round things off.

traditional_dishes.name: Sarmale (Romanian Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
traditional_dishes.note: Cabbage rolls filled with meat and rice, Romania's version of sarma.

traditional_dishes.name: Mămăligă (Romanian Cornmeal Porridge)
traditional_dishes.note: Cornmeal porridge, a traditional stand-in for bread.

traditional_dishes.name: Mici (Romanian Grilled Meat Rolls)
traditional_dishes.note: Grilled ground-meat rolls made without casing.

must_try.name: Sarmale (Romanian Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
must_try.note: Cabbage rolls filled with meat and rice, served with sour cream.

must_try.name: Mămăligă (Romanian Cornmeal Porridge)
must_try.note: Cornmeal porridge, often with cheese and sour cream.

must_try.name: Mici (Romanian Grilled Meat Rolls)
must_try.note: Grilled ground-meat rolls with mustard and bread.

must_try.name: Ciorbă de Burtă (Romanian Tripe Soup)
must_try.note: A sour tripe soup with sour cream and garlic.

must_try.name: Papanași (Romanian Cottage Cheese Doughnuts)
must_try.note: Fried curd-cheese dumplings with jam and sour cream.

fun_facts: Mămăligă was traditionally sliced with thread instead of a knife, and in leaner times it stood in for bread on the rural table.
Mici are grilled without a casing — legend has it they were invented when a Bucharest innkeeper ran out of sausage casing and simply shaped the meat into rolls.

countries.title: Bulgaria
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Bulgarian cuisine is known for its vegetable salads, grilled meat, and yogurt — still made in the country according to old tradition.
countries.taste_intro: Fresh vegetables, sirene cheese, and plenty of grilled meat, all rounded out with the cultured milk on which Bulgaria has built its reputation.

traditional_dishes.name: Shopska Salad (Shopska Salata)
traditional_dishes.note: A tomato salad with cucumber, pepper, and grated sirene cheese.

traditional_dishes.name: Banitsa (Bulgarian Cheese Pastry)
traditional_dishes.note: Phyllo pastry filled with cheese and eggs, a classic Bulgarian breakfast.

traditional_dishes.name: Kavarma (Bulgarian Braised Meat)
traditional_dishes.note: Braised meat with vegetables in a clay dish.

must_try.name: Shopska salad

must_try.name: Kavarma (Bulgarian Braised Meat)

fun_facts: Bulgarian yogurt is linked to the bacterium Lactobacillus bulgaricus, named directly after the country where it was first described.
Shopska salad is named after the Šopluk region around Sofia and is traditionally served as a starter before the main course.

countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: British cuisine is the cuisine of the Sunday roast and fried food from the sea — simple, hearty, with a generous sauce on top.
countries.taste_intro: Crispy fried fish, a juicy roast with gravy, and a hot pudding with syrup to finish — British food is comforting, not showy.

traditional_dishes.name: Fish and Chips
traditional_dishes.note: Battered fried fish with chips, a classic from the English coast.

traditional_dishes.name: Beef Wellington
traditional_dishes.note: Beef tenderloin in puff pastry with mushroom duxelles.

traditional_dishes.name: Yorkshire Pudding
traditional_dishes.note: A puffed batter bake, traditional with the Sunday roast.

must_try.name: Sticky Toffee Pudding

fun_facts: Fish and chips spread across Britain in the 19th century as cheap, quick food for workers in port and industrial towns.
Yorkshire pudding is traditionally baked in a very hot oven for exactly this reason: to puff up into its airy, domed shape.

countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Irish cuisine comes from what grows well in a damp, cool climate — potatoes, cabbage, and lamb make food for cold days.
countries.taste_intro: Meat braised with root vegetables, mashed potato mixed with cabbage, and a quick soda bread without yeast — Irish cooking is rural and simple.

traditional_dishes.name: Irish Stew
traditional_dishes.note: Lamb braised with potatoes and root vegetables.

traditional_dishes.name: Colcannon
traditional_dishes.note: Mashed potato with kale or cabbage and butter.

traditional_dishes.name: Irish Soda Bread
traditional_dishes.note: A quick bread leavened with baking soda instead of yeast.

fun_facts: Irish soda bread has been baked without yeast since the mid-19th century, when baking soda arrived in Ireland as an affordable leavening agent.
Colcannon was traditionally served on Halloween, when small coins or a ring were hidden inside for good luck.

countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Swedish cuisine lives on potatoes, fish, and foraged berries — simple Nordic food rounded out by the ritual of an afternoon coffee break and a cinnamon bun.
countries.taste_intro: Lightly sweet, seasoned with lingonberries and dill, with a salty edge from cured salmon — Swedish food is balanced and calm, never fiery.

traditional_dishes.note: Meatballs with mashed potato and lingonberry sauce.

traditional_dishes.note: Salmon cured in salt, sugar, and dill.

traditional_dishes.name: Kanelbullar (Swedish Cinnamon Buns)
traditional_dishes.note: Yeasted buns with a cinnamon filling, a symbol of Swedish fika.

must_try.name: Swedish meatballs

must_try.name: Gravlax (Cured Salmon)
must_try.note: Salmon cured in salt, sugar, and dill.

must_try.name: Janssons frestelse
must_try.note: Baked potatoes with anchovies and cream.

must_try.name: Kanelbullar
must_try.note: Cinnamon buns for the afternoon fika.

must_try.name: Toast Skagen (Swedish Shrimp Toast)
must_try.note: Toast with a shrimp salad and fish roe.

fun_facts: The Swedish "fika" — an afternoon break for coffee and something sweet — is so deeply rooted it's treated almost as a social obligation.
Köttbullar became famous outside Sweden largely thanks to the furniture chain IKEA's cafeterias, though the traditional recipe is much older.

countries.title: Norway
countries.facts_source: Worldometer.info (odhad na základě dat OSN), zaokrouhleno
countries.intro: Norwegian cuisine belongs to the sea and the mountains — fish, lamb, and potatoes form the backbone of a country with a long coastline and a short summer.
countries.taste_intro: Fresh and preserved fish, lamb with cabbage, and plenty of potatoes — Norwegian food is simple and doesn't hide its harsher climate.

traditional_dishes.note: Lamb braised with cabbage and whole peppercorns, Norway's national dish.

traditional_dishes.note: A creamy fish soup with vegetables.

traditional_dishes.name: Lefse (Norwegian Potato Flatbread)
traditional_dishes.note: Thin potato flatbread, traditional at Christmas.

must_try.name: Fårikål (Norwegian Lamb and Cabbage Stew)

must_try.name: Norwegian meat cakes

must_try.name: Fiskekaker (Norwegian Fish Cakes)
must_try.note: Fish cakes made from cod or haddock.

fun_facts: Fårikål has been officially declared Norway's national dish since 2019, and it even has its own "fårikål day" at the end of September.
Lefse is traditionally baked on a special round griddle and, at Christmas, filled with butter, sugar, or cinnamon.
